49ceac45ecbe: Salesforce Utilization Heatmap: See Who Is Overbooked
ba5f9ffbf513: A Salesforce utilization heatmap: each resource down the side, every day showing booked against capacity, overbooking flagged, one click into the schedule.
0fab20332424: How do I see resource utilization in Salesforce?
911717b994f4: Standard Salesforce has no utilization view for your own booking objects; you would build a report per question. MultiDatePick adds a Utilization view to the calendar component: each resource is a row, each day a cell showing booked against that resource's capacity, with a combined row for the whole group and an average and open count on the right.
89b6fa3623ed: What does a cell like 2/2 or 3/4 mean?
5b9feb9a4a86: Bookings on that day against the resource's capacity. 3/4 means three of four places are taken. The darker the blue, the fuller the day, and a day booked past capacity gets an orange ring so it stands out.
e296bb2070c1: What if my resource object has no capacity field?
d47aef9f25a5: The heatmap still works. Cells show a plain count of bookings on the same blue scale, and a note under the grid says so. Add a number field for capacity whenever you want percentages and open places instead.
4a6dac7a0485: Can I book or edit from the Utilization view?
400318fca92a: Utilization is read only by design: it answers how full things are. Click any booked cell and the component opens that resource's week on that day, where you can book, move or edit.
03121cffd8ba: Can the rows be people instead of rooms?
a9ce3a57077e: Yes. The resource can be any object, including User. Add a capacity number to User and the heatmap becomes a team capacity dashboard: who is full, who has room, and which weeks are overloaded.
98c6e86974e8: Salesforce utilization heatmap for advisor appointments: each advisor's daily bookings shown as booked of capacity, a combined availability row across the top and an average and open column on the right
b77aeb69e050: Salesforce utilization heatmap of multi-day client engagements: three advisors with a capacity of two engagements each, a full month across, showing which days each advisor is fully committed
0d267e80e2b3: The Salesforce Utilization Heatmap: See Who Is Overbooked
693985d90843: Every room, person or asset down the side, every day across the top, and each cell showing how much of its capacity is booked. A capacity dashboard for your own Salesforce objects, set up without code.
d734f4544ff1: "Is the team overbooked next week?" "Which room sits empty most of the month?" "Can we take on one more engagement?" Those are capacity questions. A calendar shows what is booked; it does not show how full anything is. A utilization heatmap does.
007ff092289c: MultiDatePick's Utilization view reads the same bookings as its calendar and timeline and turns them into a grid of fill levels: one row per resource, one cell per day, each cell saying how many of that resource's places are taken. It is one config field away from any placement, and it needs nothing more than a number on the resource for capacity.
874a219a5cf6: Advisors down the side, booked of capacity in every cell. Hover a day for its bookings, click it to open that week.
4a0ed46d14a4: Each cell reads like 3/4: three of four places taken. The fuller the day, the darker the blue.
300643871933: A day booked past capacity gets an orange ring. It is never quietly capped at "full".
052de1930414: A row across the top shows the whole group's fill per day as a percentage, so the crunch days stand out.
68b9ed46d181: The right-hand column gives each resource's average for the month and how many places are still open from today.
1ff77ac1b40d: Click a booked cell and the component opens that resource's week on that day, ready to book or edit.
d3ab10e0a4a0: No capacity field yet? Cells show a plain count of bookings on the same scale, and the grid says so.
a48d26bb3763: A month of capacity in one look
cb04bc125330: Reports can tell you utilization, one question at a time. The heatmap shows the whole month at once, so patterns jump out that a report would never surface: the advisor who is full every Tuesday, the room nobody books on Fridays, the week where everyone is at capacity at the same time. The grid opens on today, keeps resource names pinned while you scroll, and counts open places only from today forward, because unused capacity last week cannot be booked anymore.
63695059f071: A month of advisor appointments. The darkest cells are full days; the right-hand column says how much room is left.
6917855bce3b: Multi-day work counts on every day it runs
e9b8de6fd220: Capacity covers more than meetings. A consultant can carry two client engagements at a time; a crew can work one job site at once; a training room hosts one course for a whole week. The heatmap counts a multi-day booking on every day it covers, so an engagement that runs Monday to Friday fills all five cells. Set the capacity to the number of things a resource can carry at once and the grid shows exactly when each person is fully committed.
6a0aa243326c: Client engagements against a capacity of two per advisor. 2/2 means fully committed that day.
